q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON WHERE NAME != ALL ( SELECT S.NAME FROM SALESPERSON S LEFT JOIN ORDERS O ON S.SALES_ID = O.SALES_ID LEFT JOIN COMPANY C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE C.NAME = 'RED')

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 selects salespersons who have zero orders associated with the company named 'RED'. Q2 selects salespersons whose name is not all equal to salespersons who have orders with the company named 'RED'. These are not logically equivalent, especially when salespersons have multiple orders or no orders at all.
counterexample_dsp: A scenario where a salesperson has no orders at all with 'RED' but Q2 incorrectly excludes them due to the ALL comparison with an empty set.
